new_articles.title: GST cuts drive 20% surge in auto sales, industry leaders say
new_articles.summary: Hyundai Motor 관련 기사다. 기사 제목은 'GST cuts drive 20% surge in auto sales, industry leaders say'이다. At Maruti Suzuki, passenger vehicle sales grew nearly 36% year-on-year between April and August 2026, with the entry-level segment surging over 96%. Hyundai Motor India echoed the trend. Hyundai Motor India echoed the trend IANS India auto sales (Image for representation) New Delhi: Auto retail sales in India jumped 20% to 3 crore vehicles in the last 11 months as GST rate cuts widened affordability and pulled first-time buyers back to showrooms, top auto industry executives said "This demonstrates the power of the Indian consumer and the importance of affordability," said Hisashi Takeuchi, Managing Director & CEO, Maruti Suzuki India Limited, adding that the company is accelerating capex plans, with a "multiplier effect across the economy" expected to follow Also read | First-time car buyers make a comeback as lower GST boosts small-vehicle demand Hyundai Motor India echoed the trend 0 reforms have been a significant catalyst for the Indian automotive industry," said Tarun Garg, MD & CEO, HMIL, noting that monthly wholesale volumes of over 4 lakh units have become "the new normal. 이 기사는 해당 기업과 연결된 해외 보도를 바탕으로 정리했다.

new_articles.title: Who needs a degree? South Korea’s chip boom rewires university-obsessed culture
new_articles.summary: Samsung Electronics, SK hynix 관련 기사다. 기사 제목은 'Who needs a degree? South Korea’s chip boom rewires university-obsessed culture'이다. Inside a brightly lit cleanroom at Chungbuk Semiconductor High School in South Korea, a group of teenagers in head-to-toe protective suits carefully handled silicon wafers, learning the same production processes used in commercial chip plants. About half of the school’s graduates head straight to large companies such as Samsung Electronics or SK Hynix without ever setting foot in a university classroom. The scene illustrates how South Korea’s semiconductor boom is beginning to challenge the. . South Korea’s chip boom rewires university-obsessed culture ‘When I think about the pay I’ll be getting at Samsung, I’m not worried at all,’ a student at a semiconductor school says 3 -MIN READ 3 -MIN Listen Kyodo Published: 2:49pm, 22 Sep 2026 Inside a brightly lit cleanroom at Chungbuk Semiconductor High School in South Korea , a group of teenagers in head-to-toe protective suits carefully handled silicon wafers, learning the same production processes used in commercial chip plants About half of the school’s graduates head straight to large companies such as Samsung Electronics or SK Hynix without ever setting foot in a university classroom The scene illustrates how South Korea’s semiconductor boom is beginning to challenge the country’s deeply entrenched belief that a university degree is the only route to a successful career Even graduates of prestigious universities struggle to land jobs at large companies that are looking for experienced workers rather than new graduates. 이 기사는 해당 기업과 연결된 해외 보도를 바탕으로 정리했다.
